summary.short: Utah Consumer Privacy Act, effective December 31, 2023. Applies to controllers and processors above revenue and consumer-count thresholds that do business in Utah or target its residents. Gives consumers access, deletion, portability and opt-out rights; imposes controller duties; enforced by the Attorney General with no private right of action.
summary.long: Enacts the Utah Consumer Privacy Act, effective December 31, 2023, for controllers and processors doing business in Utah or targeting Utah residents, with annual revenue of $25,000,000 or more and personal data of 100,000 or more consumers controlled or processed in a calendar year (or 25,000 or more consumers where over 50% of gross revenue comes from selling personal data). Excludes governmental entities, covered entities, nonprofits, higher education institutions and certain financial institutions. Consumers may confirm processing, access, delete, port and opt out of targeted advertising and sale of their personal data. Controllers must respond within 45 days (extendable once by 45 days), provide a privacy notice, maintain reasonable data security, give notice and an opt-out opportunity before processing sensitive data, not discriminate against consumers exercising rights, and bind processors by contract. The Division of Consumer Protection takes complaints and refers them to the Attorney General, who has exclusive enforcement authority after a 30-day cure notice and may recover actual damages and up to $7,500 per violation. No private right of action is created. A report on enforcement is due before July 1, 2025.
